subject: Chemistry
title: Polysaccharides: Amylose, Amylopectin, Cellulose, & Glycogen
topics: 4. Polysaccharide Overview: Storage Polysaccharides (Starch, Glycogen) vs Structural Polysaccharides (Cellulose)
4.1 Amylose (15–20% of Starch): Linear Unbranched α-(1→4) Glucan Helix, Water-Soluble, Blue-Black Iodine Complex
Amylopectin (80–85% of Starch): Linear α-(1→4) with α-(1→6) Branch Points every 24–30 Units, Red-Violet with Iodine
Cellulose: Linear Unbranched β-(1→4) Glucan Chains with Inter-Chain Hydrogen Bonds, Insoluble, Gives NO Color with Iodine
Glycogen ("Animal Starch"): Highly Branched α-(1→4) with α-(1→6) Branches every 8–12 Units, Red-Brown with Iodine
quickSummary: Starch consists of water-soluble Amylose [linear α-(1→4) helix trapping I₂ to give deep blue-black color] and water-insoluble Amylopectin [linear α-(1→4) with α-(1→6) branches every 24–30 units]. Cellulose is an unbranched linear β-(1→4) polymer forming rigid H-bonded microfibrils that gives NO color with iodine and is indigestible in humans. Glycogen is animal starch with α-(1→6) branches every 8–12 units.
summary: Master polysaccharide branching architectures, glycosidic linkages, and iodine test diagnostic responses.

summaryBox.title: Polysaccharide Linkages & Iodine Colors
summaryBox.takeaway: Amylose: α-(1→4) ──► Blue-black. Amylopectin: α-(1→4) + α-(1→6) branches (24–30) ──► Red-violet. Cellulose: β-(1→4) ──► No color. Glycogen: α-(1→4) + α-(1→6) branches (8–12) ──► Red-brown.

quickRevision: Amylose: linear α-(1→4) helix; water-soluble; deep blue-black with iodine.
Amylopectin: α-(1→4) with α-(1→6) branches every 24–30 units; red-violet with iodine.
Cellulose: linear β-(1→4) unbranched glucan; gives NO color with iodine.
Humans lack cellulase enzymes to cleave β-(1→4) glycosidic bonds.
Glycogen: animal starch with α-(1→6) branches every 8–12 units.
